title: A Cohen ring modulo p^n is formally smooth over Z/p^n
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ which is $p\Lambda$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]). Then for every $n\ge1$ the ring map $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is formally smooth (the case $\mathfrak n=0$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]). Explicitly, since a $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$-algebra is a ring in which $p^n=0$ and every ring homomorphism between such rings is $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$-linear: for every commutative ring $D$ with $p^nD=0$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and every ring homomorphism $g:\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to D/J$, there is a ring homomorphism $f:\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.
